## Design note

The highway-patrol hunter: the fastest police unit on open road and the only one that can sit on a sports car's bumper flat out. No push bar, and the pursuit 5.0 has the power to drag a full light bar to the top of the roster. In town it is the same handful as the civilian coupe — traction-limited off the line, heavy nose into corners — so it is a poor boxing-in car; it wins on the motorway, not in the grid.

## How this car breaks

A civilian muscle-coupe shell with heavy-duty cooling and suspension parts, but no push bar and no reinforced bumper: the long nose and big cooling pack fold in any committed ram, and the wide doors dent easily. Built to chase, not to shove — it loses to the Cruiser and the SUVs in every contact.

## Sources (type)

- fleet spec-class data for 2010s highway-patrol pursuit coupes
- owner dyno averages for later-generation NA 5.0 DOHC V8s
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, multi-piston caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 872 | 0.80 | 700 |
| pitch | 3859 | 0.90 | 3470 |
| yaw | 4125 | 0.92 | 3800 |

## Engine

5.0 L DOHC 32-valve V8, naturally aspirated, later high-compression generation, pursuit calibration. Class-typical late-2010s NA 5.0 V8 (~69 kW/L, ~344 kW at 7000 rpm, ~560 N·m at 4600) per spec-class data and owner dynos — the later generation of the Rampart's engine family, which is what highway-patrol pursuit coupes carried.

## Drivetrain

6-speed automatic with torque converter (pursuit calibration: firm, late shifts), clutch-type rear LSD. Layout **RWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 40 N·m, power ramp 0.40, coast ramp 0.30. Torque converter: stall 2500 rpm, 1.9× at stall, couples 1:1 from 2900 rpm (class-typical for the gearbox). Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 900 N·m. Shift time 0.28 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.17 | 14.80 | 63 |
| 2 | 2.34 | 8.31 | 112 |
| 3 | 1.52 | 5.40 | 173 |
| 4 | 1.14 | 4.05 | 230 |
| 5 | 0.87 | 3.09 | 302 |
| 6 | 0.69 | 2.45 | 380 |

Final drive 3.55, reverse 3.40. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.341 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.31 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 474 kg | 1.60 Hz | 47900 N/m | 2960 N·s/m | 4440 N·s/m | 0.15 m |
| Rear | 398 kg | 1.70 Hz | 45400 N/m | 2640 N·s/m | 3960 N·s/m | 0.16 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 2.6°/g with 64% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.412 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 164816 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 59809 F / 61817 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **18300 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 2.6°/g, front share 63%. Bump stops 180000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -0.8° F / -1.0° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 46 mm + 40 mm + 36 mm → A = 39.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·39.4 cm²·0.165 m = **5456 N·m**
- Rear: 330 mm disc, pistons per side 45 mm → A = 15.9 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 140 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·15.9 cm²·0.140 m = **1781 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 5456 / 1781 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.14), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.69 → **3760 / 1230 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 2201 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.71×), rear needs 844 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.46×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 1441 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 3760 N·m front / 1230 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1430 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 15.7:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 10.4 m → outer-front path radius 5.07 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.49 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.662 rad (37.9°)** (outer 32.4°, inner 45.2° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.60). Rack speed 1.4 rad/s.
